lots.what_it_is: Low rectangular pegged trestle coffee table (catalogued as Arts and Crafts English oak peg), plank top with moulded edge, two shaped waisted trestle ends each with a cross-shaped tusk/key peg through the stretcher tenon, plinth feet, single central stretcher. Unmarked; age and timber not proven from photos.

sold.date: listed 2026-06-09, sold about a week later
sold.note: Page opened (API record and photo checked). 'OAK ARTS & CRAFTS STYLE SIDE TABLE': round-top pegged oak side table with slab legs and shaped rail, worn top. Same style and pegged construction, different form (round side table, not a trestle coffee table). Hammer, premium extra. No rate needed.

Page opened, photo checked. 'OAK COFFEE TABLE': modern Tasmanian oak open box coffee table with lower shelf. Not Arts and Crafts or trestle; shows what a solid oak coffee table brings in Tasmania. Hammer, premium extra.

Page opened, photo checked. 'OAK STRETCHER BASE TABLE': dark 1930s-style oak refectory-type table on turned end supports with stretcher, taller and larger. Structural cousin only. Hammer, premium extra.

Page opened, photo checked. 'OAK COFFEE TABLE': in fact a plain glossy Tasmanian oak trestle-form coffee table with plank ends and a wavy stretcher, no pegged joints. Closer in form than the researcher said, but a plain modern piece. Shows the trestle form alone carries no premium. Hammer, premium extra.

Page opened, photo checked. 'SINGLE DRAWER TASMANIAN OAK COFFEE TABLE': plain rectangular coffee table with drawer, square legs. Top of the range for oak coffee tables at Gowans in the last year (others $10 to $130 hammer, e.g. 396957 $10, 412633 $130, 413600 $110). Hammer, premium extra.

asking.note: Page opened. 'Antique Oak Arts and Crafts Coffee Side Table, c 1920': solid oak, bevelled plank top, trestle base with pegs, central stretcher, 119 x 45 x 46 cm, good order. Very close in form to this lot. UK retail asking with dealer margin, 'call for availability', not a price paid. Rate about 1.96 AUD per GBP (approximate, not checked).

lots.guide_summary: Only two close entries survive: one SOLD ($220 hammer at Gowans for a pegged oak Arts and Crafts style side table, different form) and one ASKING (GBP 250, about AUD 490, UK dealer retail for a near-identical c1920 pegged oak trestle coffee table). No UNSOLD. Category guide SOLD results for ordinary oak coffee tables at Gowans run $10 to $160 hammer, and a plain trestle-form oak coffee table made only $26, so the realistic Tasmanian auction value is probably $80 to $200 unless it is genuinely period English oak. GBP at about 1.96 AUD (approximate).
lots.working: No same-item SOLD evidence: no pegged trestle coffee table of this type found sold at Armitage, Gowans or elsewhere in the last 24 months. The $220 Gowans sale is close in style but a different form, and the other Gowans sales are ordinary oak coffee tables. Rules require same-item SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For reference only (not a maximum): if the $220 close sale were treated as a resale value, flip would be (220 less about 15% fees and $0 postage for local pickup = 187) / 2.44 = 76, and keep 220 / 1.22 = 180; set aside because the comparison is not the same item. Armitage premium 22% incl GST.
lots.confidence_reason: No mark or label to read, timber and age unproven from two photos, no same-item SOLD entries; rests on one close SOLD of a different form and one overseas asking price.

Gowans 366466 'RUSTIC COFFEE TABLE' $35: live-edge slab on log base, not comparable form; dropped. Gowans 413416 'MID-CENTURY OAK COFFEE TABLE' $25 (bundled by researcher with 413292): mid-century table on tapered legs, not comparable; dropped. Note: further WebSearch (including site:armitage.bidsonline.com.au) was not possible this run because the search budget was used up, so Armitage's own past results were not checked.
lots.key_photo_findings: Two photos from either end. Pegged trestle construction with cross-shaped tusk keys through the stretcher tenons on both ends, waisted shaped uprights with arched cut-outs, plinth feet, moulded top edge. Grain shows some figure that could be oak but medullary ray fleck is not clear at this resolution; colour is a light golden finish, fairly even. Top shows light scratches and small marks, no obvious splits. A dark curved object is visible under the top at one end (possibly a bracket or something stored underneath). No maker's label, stamp or retailer mark visible; underside not photographed.
lots.condition: Appears sound and complete from the photos, light surface wear to top, finish even (possibly refinished). Underside, joints and timber unconfirmed.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is it solid oak (quarter-sawn fleck visible?) and does it look genuinely early 20th century English rather than a later reproduction or Australian copy? Any label or stamp underneath, what is under the top at one end, are the joints tight, and what are the dimensions?
